title: Landau Windows — same theorem, fewer assumptions

segments.chapter: A closer look at step two
segments.text: The reference video makes a striking point: a ceiling alone is enough. This project takes a closer look at that bridge. Can we prove it with fewer foundational assumptions?

There are three steps in the picture. Reflect the zeros. Turn a ceiling into a zero free region. Then construct the ceiling. Landau Windows studies the middle step. We are extracting a classical theorem, rather than claiming a proof of the Riemann hypothesis.

Here, the ceiling is available on recurring windows. A zero beyond the target line forces violations in sufficiently large windows. The effective version must do more than say that a violation exists. It must compute an address, and certify the inequality there using finite arithmetic. The curve shown here is a schematic.

Lean checks the classical mathematics in a powerful foundation. Its universe hierarchy has standard consistency models using inaccessible cardinals. That does not show this number theory needs those cardinals. Our target is an arithmetic proof in A C L two, with a precise interpretation at roughly Peano arithmetic strength.

segments.chapter: Formulation is only a starting point
segments.text: The Riemann hypothesis has elementary arithmetic formulations. That makes weaker foundations a meaningful research question. It does not guarantee that Peano arithmetic can prove it. Each piece needs an actual proof, and the mathematical connection between formulations must also be justified.

Why care? Under the usual hypotheses, a consistent effective theory containing enough arithmetic cannot prove its own consistency. A stronger theory can sometimes prove the consistency of a weaker one. Z F C can prove the consistency of Peano arithmetic. Reducing a theorem's assumptions makes its foundational commitment smaller.

We already have the classical Landau result checked in Lean. In A C L two, we have certified arithmetic evaluators, finite window searches, explicit thresholds, and transport bounds. The analytic coefficient argument, general zero covers, and full composition are still being developed. This is a progress draft.

The destination is the full Landau reduction in A C L two, together with its mathematical interpretation. A sound checker is one component. We also need a proof that the search succeeds under the intended hypotheses. That is how we chip away at the foundations, one theorem at a time.
